_meta.purpose: Detection-fix eval: query-contaminated wrong-part cases. The prior synthetic evals hit 100% and BOTH failed on the first real input because they tested clean cases and missed query-contaminated ones. This dataset exists to CATCH the live bug (a pump page ranked #1 above seals at 46%) before any fix is applied.
_meta.the_bug: On 'Goulds 3196 mechanical seal', a PUMP (Pumpman, opaque URL shoppumps.com/category-s/355.htm) ranked #1 at 46% above real seals. Root cause: opaque URL -> detection falls back to text; the page text echoes the query term ('mechanical seal' / 'seal kit'); classify_noun_class is longest-synonym-first, so 'mechanical seal' (len 15) beat 'pump' (len 4) -> result classified SEAL -> same-class gate ~1.0 -> pump not crushed.

result.vendor: string (the vendor name — a corroborating signal for the fix)
result.snippet: string (page text; contaminated cases echo the query noun)
result.title: string?

expected.expected_noun_class: string | null (the class a correct detector SHOULD assign to the result)

_meta.note: The live_failure case (pumpman_pump_seal_kit_page) MUST wrongly-pass against the CURRENT (unfixed) code — that is the bug reproduced in the eval. If it does not wrongly-pass, the eval is not testing the real bug and we fix the eval before touching any code. expected_noun_class is the verdict a CORRECT dominant-class detector would reach (PUMP for a pump page, even if it mentions a seal). The residual_uncorroborated_opaque_pump case is a documented known-gap: a wrong-part result with an opaque URL AND an unclassifiable vendor/domain — the structural-signal fix cannot reach it, so it will STILL wrongly pass after the fix. It is NOT relabeled and the fix is NOT stretched to catch it; the flywheel sizes that residual with real data.

result.snippet: Goulds 3196 pump with mechanical seal kit. Pumpman industrial pump distributor. In stock, ships today. Cross-reference available.
result.title: Goulds 3196 Pump - Pumpman

expected.rationale: THE LIVE BUG. A Goulds 3196 PUMP listing on Pumpman (opaque URL /category-s/355.htm, no slug). The page text mentions 'mechanical seal kit' (echoing the seal-led query). Current detector: longest-synonym-first -> 'mechanical seal' (15) beats 'pump' (4) -> SEAL -> same-class gate ~1.0 -> survives at ~46%. CORRECT verdict: the vendor 'Pumpman' + domain 'shoppumps.com' + 'pump distributor' all say PUMP; the 'seal kit' is incidental. Must be classified PUMP and crushed (different class) below floor. expected should_pass_floor=FALSE.

result.snippet: Goulds 3196 centrifugal pump. Mechanical seal replacement available. In stock at Zoro. Free shipping.

expected.rationale: Contaminated pump-on-seal. URL slug /pump/centrifugal/ says PUMP, but snippet also says 'Mechanical seal replacement' (query echo). Current detector: URL-wins-on-disagreement -> PUMP (URL slug present) -> gate 0.1 -> crushed. This case should ALREADY fail correctly (URL slug saves it) — included to confirm the URL-slug path works and contrast with the opaque-URL Pumpman cases that don't.

result.snippet: Goulds 3196 pump with mechanical seal. In stock, ships today. MB Glick industrial supply.
result.title: Goulds 3196 Pump - MB Glick

expected.rationale: RESIDUAL KNOWN-GAP (do NOT relabel, do NOT stretch the fix). A pump page with an OPAQUE URL (/products/g3196-pump-unit — no part-type slug the dictionary reads, NOT a collection page) AND an UNCLASSIFIABLE vendor/domain ('MB Glick' / 'mbglick.com' carry no noun-class). The structural-signal fix cannot reach it (no vendor/domain class to override the snippet echo), so it STILL wrongly passes after the fix (snippet 'mechanical seal' -> SEAL -> same-class gate ~1.0 -> base survives the floor). This is the honest residual: uncorroborated opaque-URL wrong-part cases remain until the flywheel sizes them with real data (Stage 3 page-fetch/LLM, out of scope). Desired verdict FALSE; reported as known-gap, not asserted.
